openai.feedback:
- Category: bug
- Severity: medium
- File: shared/scripts/tools/verifiers/_tag_binding_py.py:181
- Finding: Scope-marker parsing ignores assignment targets other than a plain name. For example, `pytestmark, unused = ([mark.covers("FR-01.11")], None)` applies a requirement marker in pytest, but this parser overlooks it and can grant a function’s `covers_none` declaration. This misses the required contradiction check across all assignment forms.
- Suggestion: Handle destructuring and subscript assignments involving `pytestmark`, or conservatively refuse infrastructure classification when such assignments cannot be resolved. Add tests using these forms with a direct `covers_none` decorator.

- Category: spec
- Severity: medium
- File: shared/scripts/tools/verifiers/tag_binding_gate.py:129
- Finding: An unreadable base catalog produces `catalog=None`, but the gate continues. Only tests declaring `covers_none` subsequently fail; a change without those declarations can pass without reporting “cannot enforce.” The specification explicitly distinguishes unreadable catalogs from absent or invalid ones.
- Suggestion: Return a “cannot enforce” failure immediately when the base catalog read returns `None`. Add a gate-level test for an unreadable catalog with no infrastructure declarations.

- Category: test
- Severity: medium
- File: shared/scripts/tools/verifiers/_tag_binding_infra_pass.py:59
- Finding: Catalog validation accepts any relative `.py` path, and the new head-catalog test checks only that the file exists. Consequently, an existing production file such as `shared/scripts/example.py` passes the promised CI validation even though it is not a test file.
- Suggestion: Extend head-catalog validation to verify that each entry identifies a test file under the repository’s collection rules. Add a negative test using an existing non-test Python file.

Ship-with-fixes. The implementation covers the main classification flow, but assignment parsing and catalog enforcement leave concrete acceptance criteria incomplete.

SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise

glm.feedback:
## Review

The change is well-built and closely tracks the spec. The core security properties hold: granting is strict (exact `pytest.mark.covers_none` with one literal valid label), the catalog is read at the merge-base only, exact paths only (no wildcards/absolut/backslash), contradiction detection is loose in the safe direction, infra tests leave the exemption denominator, and the digest ignores only the exact marker shape. Marker registration is applied everywhere `covers` is registered. Test coverage is genuinely behavioral (hand-built manifests plus real-git integration tests, happy and error paths both present).

Findings:

- Category: spec | Severity: low
  File: `shared/config/infra_test_paths.json` (absent from the diff)
  Finding: The Design Notes say the catalog is seeded with the six existing testkit meta-test files, but no catalog file is created in this diff; the head-catalog CI test (`test_the_head_catalog_is_valid_and_names_existing_files`) self-skips while the file is absent, and the CODEOWNERS line guards a path that does not yet exist. The glm bootstrap review notes say this deferral is deliberate ("no seed file is touched in this run; retag is a follow-up merge"), so this is a disclosed deviation rather than a hole — the bootstrap test `test_without_a_catalog_at_base...` proves nothing is granted meanwhile.
  Suggestion: Ship as-is, but make sure the follow-up merge that creates the seed catalog is actually tracked; otherwise the "guarded by CODEOWNERS" claim is vacuous until then.

- Category: bug | Severity: low
  File: `shared/scripts/tools/verifiers/_tag_binding_infra_pass.py` — `_correction` / `classify`
  Finding: `_correction` appends the "drops stand-in tag" WARNING the moment a correction is accepted, but `_refuse_quiet_loss` runs afterwards and can demote the same test to `bad-infra-class` (e.g. an unrelated tagged test vanished in the same change). The gate output then simultaneously reports a hard finding for the test *and* a WARNING that it "drops stand-in tag (reclassified as infrastructure)" — contradictory/misleading operator output.
  Suggestion: Move the warning emission to after `_refuse_quiet_loss`, or have `_refuse_quiet_loss` retract the warnings belonging to tests it demotes.

- Category: edge-case | Severity: low
  File: `shared/scripts/tools/verifiers/_tag_binding_infra_pass.py` — `_verdict`
  Finding: For a newly added test sitting next to a module-level `covers_none` alongside same-name siblings, the `is_new and not all(i.direct ...)` check fires first and reports "needs its own @pytest.mark.covers_none", masking the sibling-disagreement reason; both are `bad-infra-class` so enforcement is unaffected — message-only imprecision.
  Suggestion: Optional: run the sibling check before the module-level check, or aggregate both reasons.

- Category: test | Severity: low
  File: `shared/tests/test_tag_binding_infra_class.py` — `test_class_level_covers_forms_and_unresolved_class_marks_contradict_the_marker`
  Finding: This case is only asserted against `py_infra_info` directly, not through `evaluate` like the other contradiction forms; a wiring mistake in `_verdict`'s `info.bad` consumption would not be caught by it. The remaining forms are covered end-to-end, so the residual risk is small.
  Suggestion: Route one of the four parametrized cases through `_run`/`evaluate` as well.

Things I specifically checked and found correct: `parse_catalog`'s three-way absent/`""`/`None` handling matches the AC and is exercised through the real gate in the integration tests; the base-vs-head differ WARNING survives a failing gate; superseded-finding filtering only removes the four listed kinds and only for decided tests; a manifest-linked test can never be classed (defense beyond the parser); a renamed+edited stand-in cannot slip the correction rule (quiet-loss check); TS/JS stays untagged; `evaluate`'s new parameter has a default, so existing callers are unaffected.

Overall: ship-as-is — the findings are refinements (one misleading-warning cleanup worth doing soon), and no loophole or correctness break in the enforcement direction was found.

SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: approve
